entries.content: I've been holding SPXL for 3 years now and it's been great. People overcomplicate this—if you're already comfortable with volatility and don't sell during dips, leveraged ETFs work in your favor. The decay everyone warns about gets offset by the compounding on up days. My returns have crushed the regular S&P. If you've proven you can sit through drawdowns, you're exactly the type of investor who benefits from these products.

Leveraged ETFs reset daily to maintain their target multiple. This daily rebalancing creates path dependency, meaning returns over periods longer than one day depend on the sequence of daily returns, not just the cumulative index return. In volatile sideways markets, this can result in value erosion even when the underlying index is flat.

For investors with several years of experience who have demonstrated discipline during market corrections, 3x leveraged S&P ETFs can serve as a straightforward way to amplify broad market exposure. Since you're tracking the S&P 500—a diversified index—you avoid single-stock concentration risk. Many experienced investors allocate a portion of their portfolio to these instruments to enhance returns without the complexity of options or margin accounts.

Speaker mentioned that for people who've held through 2022's drawdown without selling, leveraged ETFs are worth considering. The behavioral edge of not panic-selling is the hard part—the math takes care of itself if you stay invested. He showed backtests where SPXL outperformed SPY over 10-year periods for patient holders. Several members in the group have added small positions and reported good results.

Risk capacity refers to an investor's objective financial ability to absorb losses without compromising essential goals like retirement, emergency funds, or debt obligations. It is distinct from risk tolerance, which measures psychological comfort with volatility. An investor may have high risk tolerance but low risk capacity if their financial situation cannot withstand significant portfolio losses.
